transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No — do not use or charge it again, even temporarily. A battery that has become hot, swollen and split is damaged and can worsen or ignite; it needs to be treated as an unsafe battery, not simply a flat or worn one. The most likely cause is an internal lithium-cell or battery-protection failure; a charger or contact fault is also possible, but it does not make this battery safe to reuse. Keep the vacuum switched off and unplugged, and arrange assessment/disposal through Shark or a qualified battery/electrical repair service rather than fitting or opening anything yourself. With it left alone, is there any burning or chemical smell, hissing, leaking liquid or smoke from the battery area?

There's a faint sweet/chemical smell near the battery this morning, but no smoke, hissing or liquid that I can see. It's still clicked into the vacuum, charger unplugged, and leaning against the kitchen cupboards next to the tea towels. It's still warm, though not as hot as last night.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The continuing warmth and sweet/chemical smell make this an active damaged-battery risk, not a battery that can be used again. Keep it switched off and do not charge or use it; it needs assessment by Shark or a qualified battery/electrical service before the vacuum is used again. Move the vacuum away from the cupboards and tea towels only if you can do so without squeezing, dropping or disturbing the swollen battery; place it on a non-combustible surface well away from people and flammable items. If it starts smoking, hissing, leaking, or gets hotter, keep clear and call 999.

candidates: Failed lithium-ion battery cells or internal battery protection fault (high)
Charging fault involving the charger or battery contacts (medium)

You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "Battery overheated while charging and is swollen with the case splitting". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
